replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Last year, I used AI tools like Wolfram Alpha for complex physics calculations. It was helpful for quick checks and visualizing data. I didn’t get anxious because it complemented my existing skills without overwhelming me.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form (ax² + bx + c = 0). Then, calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If it’s positive, there are two real roots; if zero, one real root; if negative, two complex roots. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f’(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Plug those x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. These points could be maxima, minima, or inflection points depending on the second derivative test.
